title: Society Master
text:
Society Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Society 
 Master 
 Purpose: 
 Maintain society registration details 
 and link societies to authorities. 
 Why it matters: 
 Society is the central entity — tenants, 
 PTS, annexures, payments and reports all reference the society. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Authority & Society Setup > Society Master 
 Fields & 
 guidance: 
 Business 
 Unit: Select the BU that owns the society. 
 Society 
 Code: Unique identifier. 
 Registration 
 Number & Date: Legal registration details. 
 Detail 
 section: Select one or more Authority records under which the society 
 is registered. 
 Rules: 
 Authorities must exist before linking. Once a society is created, 
 linked authority data should not be changed lightly. 
 Best practice: 
 Use a naming convention (BU_SocietyCode) 
 to avoid duplicates.

title: List Master
text:
List Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 List Master 
 Purpose: 
 Create standardized lists used in 
 document handling and workflows (document types, annexure lists, etc.). 
 Why it matters: 
 Predefined lists reduce manual errors 
 and ensure consistent workflow behavior. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Document & Workflow Setup > List Master 
 Fields & 
 guidance: 
 Code 
 & Description — unique identifiers. 
 List 
 Type — choose the system-defined type carefully (affects downstream 
 behavior). 
 CTS 
 details — fill if required by your process. 
 Common 
 pitfall: Selecting wrong list type will mis-classify documents and 
 break automation.

title: Authority Master
text:
Authority Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Authority 
 Master 
 Purpose: 
 Register governing bodies (municipal, 
 government, regulatory) under which societies are legally registered. 
 Why it matters: 
 Societies must be tied to a valid 
 authority for legal compliance and traceability. Once an authority is 
 used in a society record it cannot be edited or deleted. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup >Authority & Society Setup > Authority Master 
 Fields & 
 guidance: 
 Authority 
 Code: Unique short code (e.g., MMB001). 
 Description: 
 Full name of the authority. 
 Save 
 behavior: After saving, the authority becomes available for Society 
 Master mapping. 
 Common 
 pitfalls: Do not create duplicate authorities; verify spelling and 
 legal name before saving.

title: Document Master
text:
Document Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Document 
 Master 
 Purpose: 
 Standardize every document type used 
 across the SRA module (identity proofs, consent forms, property papers, 
 buyout agreements, allotment letters, invoices, certificates). 
 Why it matters: 
 Accurate Document Master entries ensure 
 documents are classified correctly, attached to the right transaction 
 lines, and routed to the correct workflow stage; missing or inconsistent 
 document types break eligibility checks and audits. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Document & Workflow Setup > Document Master 
 F ields: Document 
 Code , Description 
 Rule / Notes: 
 Document Code must be unique; once 
 referenced in transactions the code/category should not be deleted; prefer 
 creating a new code for semantic changes rather than editing an existing 
 one.

title: Stage Master
text:
Stage Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Stage Master 
 Purpose: 
 Define lifecycle stages (e.g., Verification, 
 Approval, Execution, Completion). 
 Why it matters: 
 Stages drive workflow routing and 
 reporting. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Document & Workflow Setup > Stage Master 
 Fields: 
 Stage Code , Description . 
 Guidance: 
 Define stages in logical order and 
 document the intended use of each stage.

title: Overview
text:
Overview 
 Overview 
 Introduction 
 Of Slum Rehabilitation 
 Authority (SRA) 
 The 
 Slum Rehabilitation Authority 
 (SRA) was established by the Government of Maharashtra in December 
 1995 under the Slum Rehabilitation Act. The primary objective is to improve 
 the living conditions of slum dwellers by providing them with better housing 
 and infrastructure. 
 Here's 
 an overview of the SRA process: 
 1) Identification and Notification of Slums 
 a. Survey 
 and Identification: Authorities conduct surveys to identify areas eligible 
 for slum rehabilitation. 
 b. Notification: 
 Identified slum areas are officially notified under relevant legislation. 
 2) Slum Redevelopment Proposal 
 a. Developer 
 Selection: Builders or developers submit proposals to redevelop slum areas. 
 b. Approval 
 of Proposal: The proposal must be approved by a certain percentage of 
 slum dwellers (often 70%). 
 3) Formation of Housing Societies 
 a. Slum 
 Dwellers Association: Slum dwellers form a cooperative housing society 
 or a registered association. 
 b. Society 
 Registration: The association is officially registered with the SRA. 
 4) Project Planning and Approval 
 a. Project 
 Proposal: The developer, in collaboration with the slum dwellers' association, 
 prepares a detailed project plan. 
 b. Approval 
 from Authorities: The proposal is submitted to various government authorities 
 for approval. 
 5) Temporary Relocation 
 a. Temporary 
 Housing: Slum dwellers are temporarily relocated to transit camps or other 
 accommodation while the redevelopment takes place. 
 b. Relocation 
 Plan: The plan ensures minimal disruption to the lives of slum dwellers. 
 6) Construction and Development 
 a. Construction: 
 The developer begins the construction of new housing units and infrastructure. 
 b. Monitoring: 
 The SRA monitors the construction process to ensure compliance with the 
 approved plan. 
 7) Allotment of Housing Units 
 a. Eligibility 
 Verification: Eligibility of slum dwellers is verified to ensure they 
 are entitled to new housing units. 
 b. Allotment 
 Process: New housing units are allotted to eligible slum dwellers. 
 8) Occupation and Rehabilitation 
 a. Occupation 
 of Units: Slum dwellers move into their new homes. 
 b. Post-Occupation 
 Support: The SRA provides support to ensure smooth transition and rehabilitation. 
 9) Regularization and Compliance 
 a. Property 
 Regularization: New housing units are regularized and necessary documentation 
 is provided to the occupants. 
 b. Compliance 
 Check: Continuous monitoring to ensure compliance with regulations and 
 standards. 
 10) Maintenance and Upkeep 
 a. Maintenance 
 Plan: A plan is established for the maintenance of the new housing complex. 
 b. Society 
 Formation: Residents form a society to manage and maintain the property. 
 Key Benefits of SRA Projects 
 1) Improved 
 Living Conditions: Better housing, sanitation, and infrastructure. 
 2) Legal 
 Ownership: Slum dwellers gain legal ownership of their homes. 
 3) Enhanced 
 Quality of Life: Access to amenities like water, electricity, and healthcare. 
 Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA) With Farvision 
 Farvision ERP is a robust 
 tool that enhances the Slum Rehabilitation Authority's (SRA) redevelopment 
 process by integrating essential functionalities such as project management, 
 compliance management, financial oversight, and automated workflows. It 
 streamlines the documentation process, ensures real-time tracking of projects, 
 and facilitates smooth communication among stakeholders. By addressing 
 the specific needs of real estate projects, Farvision minimizes errors, 
 controls costs, and accelerates the transition of slum dwellers to their 
 new homes, thus ensuring a more efficient and transparent redevelopment 
 process.

title: Payment Head Master
text:
Payment Head Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Payment 
 Head Master 
 Purpose: 
 Define detailed payment heads and 
 link them to accounting heads. 
 Why it matters: 
 Ensures each payment is mapped to 
 the correct ledger and TDS rules are applied. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Payment Configuration > Payment Head Master 
 F ields & guidance: 
 Code 
 & Description — unique. 
 Payment 
 Head Type — select from Payment Head Type. 
 Account 
 Head — choose the GL account for posting. 
 TDS 
 Applicable — default true; change only if required. 
 Best practice: 
 Coordinate with Finance to ensure 
 correct GL mapping.

title: Payment Head Type
text:
Payment Head Type 
 Help > Setup" />
 Payment 
 Head Type 
 Purpose: 
 Define high-level categories of expenses 
 (e.g., Rent, Legal, Development). 
 Why it matters: 
 Payment Head Types are the parent 
 categories used to group payment heads and drive accounting mapping. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Payment Configuration > Payment Head Type 
 Fields: 
 Code , Description .

title: Payment Schedule Master
text:
Payment Schedule Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Payment 
 Schedule Master 
 Why 
 is it important? 
 Payment 
 Schedule Master is created t o 
 provide and manage the payment schedule details for the various 
 types of expenses or vendor services. Key 
 features include the ability to schedule recurring payments (e.g., weekly, 
 monthly). 
 The 
 Payment Schedule Master aids in cash flow management and enhances vendor 
 relationships by ensuring timely payments, thus fostering collaboration 
 and trust. 
 It 
 also improves operational efficiency and financial forecasting by reducing 
 manual intervention, minimizing errors, and providing a clear overview 
 of upcoming payments. 
 Use Case Example 
 One pertinent 
 example is the use of the Payment Schedule Master for cleaning services . 
 In this scenario, a company hires a cleaning service provider to maintain 
 the premises. The Payment Schedule Master is configured to process monthly 
 payments based on a contract that specifies the services rendered each 
 month. By creating a vendor record for the cleaning service, the company 
 ensures timely payments. 
 Steps: 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Payment Configuration > Payment Schedule Master 
 Fields & 
 guidance: 
 Template 
 Code & Name — unique. 
 Payment 
 Head Details: Add payment heads, basis, and amounts. The entered amount 
 is treated as original and default modified amount. 
 Tip: 
 Create templates for common scenarios (rent, buyout, brokerage) to 
 speed voucher creation.

title: Ward Master
text:
Ward Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Ward Master 
 Purpose: 
 The Ward Master maintains a list of 
 wards under a municipality or municipal corporation, aiding in the organisation 
 and management of these areas within the SRA module. 
 Why is Ward Master Important? 
 The Ward 
 Master enhances efficiency in area management by simplifying the identification 
 and categorization of slum regions, streamlining project tracking for 
 rehabilitation and urban development. Each ward’s unique identity minimizes 
 location management errors, improving operational accuracy. 
 Use Case Scenario 
 Consider a municipal 
 corporation initiating a slum rehabilitation project in a large city where 
 several slum clusters are dispersed across different wards. Each ward 
 needs to be tracked individually to monitor progress, allocate funds, 
 and communicate with local residents effectively. 
 In this scenario, 
 the city administration employs the Ward Master feature in the system 
 to assign unique identities to each slum cluster. 
 Steps to Create a Ward Master 
 Navigate: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Authority & Society Setup> Ward Master 
 F ields: Ward 
 Code , Description . 
 Tip: 
 Keep naming consistent (e.g., “Ward-South-01”).

title: Committee Member Master
text:
Committee Member Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 Committee 
 Member Master 
 Purpose: 
 Maintain committee member details 
 for each society. 
 Why it matters: 
 Committee members are responsible 
 for approvals and coordination; their contact details are used for notifications. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Setup > Committee Configuration > Committee Master 
 F ields: Business 
 Unit , Society , Member Name , Phone Number . 
 Rule: 
 Society must exist before adding committee 
 members.

title: SRA Generic Master
text:
SRA Generic Master 
 Help > Setup" />
 SRA Generic 
 Master 
 The SRA Generic 
 Master streamlines the transaction process for flat allotment. This 
 master setup serves as a centralised reference point for managing and 
 processing transactions related to the allotment of flats, ensuring consistency 
 across the system. 
 During 
 an audit, the company can easily retrieve a comprehensive list of all 
 flat allotment transactions recorded through the SRA Generic Master, ensuring 
 compliance with regulatory standards. 
 Purpose: Standardize unit identifiers 
 (flat numbers, floor numbers) used across Plain Table Survey (PTS) and 
 Annexure. 
 Why it matters: Prevents duplicate unit numbers and ensures consistent 
 unit references. 
 Where: 
 SRA 
 > Setup > Generic Setup > SRA Generic Master

title: Document Receipt
text:
Document Receipt 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Document 
 Receipt 
 Purpose: 
 Capture and track documents received 
 from tenants (IDs, consent forms, property papers). 
 Why it matters: 
 Document Receipt provides evidence 
 for eligibility and audit trails. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Enrollment > Document Receipt 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Header: 
 Select Business Unit, Financial Year, Document Type, Document Date. 
 Detail: 
 For each unit, record Document Type, Received Date, Stage (from Stage 
 Master). 
 Attachments: 
 Upload scanned copies of documents. 
 Save. 
 Best practice: 
 Use consistent file naming and attach 
 documents to the correct unit line to avoid mismatches during eligibility 
 checks.

title: PTS
text:
PTS 
 Help > Transaction" />
 PTS 
 Plain Table Survey (PTS) 
 The Plain Table Survey (PTS) creates 
 detailed maps of slum areas using basic surveying tools to collect comprehensive 
 data on residents and amenities. It serves as a foundational tool for 
 urban planners and social workers to assess and improve living conditions 
 in underserved communities. 
 Why 
 is PTS Important? 
 The primary purpose of the PTS is to 
 gather essential information about living conditions in slum areas, helping 
 to identify areas needing improvement and inform rehabilitation planning. 
 By providing targeted interventions based on accurate data, the PTS plays 
 a vital role in enhancing living standards and supporting community development. 
 Use Case Scenario 
 A local government identifies a slum 
 area with inadequate housing, poor sanitation, and lack of essential services. 
 They conduct a Plain Table Survey, mapping the area and gathering demographic 
 data. The survey reveals critical deficiencies, leading to a rehabilitation 
 plan for new sanitation facilities, improved housing, and clean water 
 access. Follow-up surveys assess the impact on residents’ quality of life. 
 In short, 
 Purpose of 
 PTS: Register units and 
 tenants for a society; create the base dataset for all tenant-level activities. 
 Why it matters: 
 PTS is the authoritative list of units 
 and payees; Annexure, eligibility, and payments depend on accurate PTS 
 data. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Enrollment > PTS (Plain Table Survey) 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Header: 
 Enter Document No. (system or manual) and PTS Detail (unique identifier). 
 Only one PTS can be created per Business Unit. 
 Detail 
 (line items): For each unit add: Society, Unit No., Tenant Name, Payee 
 Name, Nominee, Address, Relationship With, Occupation Status, Type 
 of Property, Agreed Carpet Area (if available). Ensure Unit No. is 
 unique within the society. 
 Attachments: 
 Attach supporting documents line-wise if required. 
 Save: 
 System may auto-create sub-ledgers (Sundry Creditors – SRA) depending 
 on backend preference TDSonSRA. Sub-ledger naming formula: Payee Name 
 + Society Name + Unit No. (used for TDS liability). 
 Rules 
 & tips: 
 PTS Detail must be unique. 
 Validate tenant names and payee names 
 carefully — these drive accounting and TDS. 
 If TDSonSRA is enabled, sub-ledgers 
 are created automatically.

title: Annexure
text:
Annexure 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Annexure 
 Purpose: 
 Create tenant-level annexure records 
 (one annexure per tenant) using PTS data; record initial eligibility status 
 and City Title Survey (CTS) details. 
 Why it matters: 
 Annexure is the tenant’s formal record 
 used for eligibility, allotment, and payments. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Annexure & Eligibility > Annexure 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Select 
 PTS No., List, Society. Default City Title Survey (CTS) details 
 populate from the selected list but can be edited. Note that the selected 
 list is sourced from the List Master. 
 Tag 
 Units: Click Select PTS and tag unit numbers that are not already 
 linked to another annexure. Units already tagged cannot be reused. 
 Annexure 
 Details: For each tenant, confirm or update tenant name, payee, area, 
 and other fields. Attach tenant-specific documents line-wise. 
 Save: 
 Annexure serial numbers are generated automatically. 
 Rules & 
 tips: 
 Each 
 tenant must have a separate annexure. 
 Annexure 
 No. must be unique. 
 Old 
 status (from PTS) and current status (can be updated) are tracked.

title: Annexure Amendment
text:
Annexure Amendment 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Annexure 
 Amendment 
 Purpose: 
 Modify previously created annexure 
 records (change consent, update documents, correct details). 
 Why it matters: 
 Tenants’ circumstances change; the 
 system must reflect accurate, current information. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Annexure & Eligibility > Annexure Amendment 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Select 
 the annexure to amend. 
 Update 
 fields (status, consent, remarks) and attach new documents if needed. 
 Save. 
 Audit: 
 Amendments should be logged with user 
 and timestamp for audit.

title: Flat Allotment
text:
Flat Allotment 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Flat Allotment 
 Purpose: 
 Finalize assignment of a permanent 
 unit to the tenant. 
 Why it matters: 
 Flat Allotment ends the tenant’s rent 
 cycle and converts temporary records into permanent allotment records. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Allotment > Flat Allotment 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Select 
 Business Unit, Financial Year, Document Type, Document Date. 
 Choose 
 Society (from Society Master) and Tenant (from Annexure). 
 Verify 
 Agreed Carpet Area (comes from PTS via Annexure) and enter Additional 
 Area if applicable. 
 Enter 
 any manual fields (remarks, special conditions). 
 Save. 
 Effect: 
 After allotment, the tenant is removed 
 from voucher generation eligibility for rent.

title: Eligibility
text:
Eligibility 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Eligibility 
 This 
 is done to determine and manage the eligibility of slum residents for 
 the rehabilitation process. 
 Eligibility 
 Criteria 
 1. Proof of 
 Residency: Residents must prove they lived in the slum before a specific 
 cut-off date (most recently January 1, 2000). 
 2. Co-operative 
 Societies: Residents must form co-operative societies. 
 3. Active Participation: 
 Residents must actively participate in the rehabilitation process. 
 Why is this Feature Important? 
 The purpose of this feature is to ensure 
 a fair and transparent process for slum rehabilitation, ensuring that 
 the benefits of rehabilitation reach the intended recipients. 
 Use Case Example 
 Let’s take an example 
 where a city government implementing a slum rehabilitation project uses 
 this feature to relocate eligible residents to newly constructed housing 
 units. The process begins with residents registering their details and 
 providing proof of residency. The system then verifies the formation of 
 co-operative societies and tracks residents’ active participation in the 
 rehabilitation process. Once the criteria are evaluated, eligible residents 
 are marked in the system, and their status is updated. 
 In short, 
 Purpose of 
 Eligibility : Update tenant 
 eligibility status when tenants provide missing or corrected documents. 
 Why it matters: 
 Eligibility determines whether a tenant 
 can receive benefits, payments, or allotment. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Annexure & Eligibility > Eligibility 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Use 
 search to find the Unit / Tenant / Annexure. 
 Select 
 the tenant and change status from Not Eligible to Eligible (or vice 
 versa). 
 Enter 
 document number and received date in the detail section. 
 Save. 
 Tip: 
 Record the reason for status change 
 in remarks for audit trail.

title: Payment Requisition Process
text:
Payment Requisition Process 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Payment 
 Requisition Process 
 Purpose: 
 Payment Requisition (PRQ) is the formal 
 request generated from Voucher Generation (or NSP) that Finance uses to 
 process actual payments (cheque, NEFT, PDC, etc.). 
 Why it matters: 
 PRQ is the bridge between SRA operational 
 payments and the Finance module. Without a valid PRQ, payments cannot 
 be executed. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Payment > Payment Requisition 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Open 
 Payment Requisition: The system auto-generates PRQs from Voucher Generation 
 or NSP. 
 Review 
 PRQ header: Check Business Unit, Document No., Payee, Amount, Payment 
 Type. 
 Validate 
 line items: Ensure each payment head, amount, and TDS deduction is 
 correct. 
 Attach 
 supporting documents: Attach invoices, approvals, and annexure references. 
 Forward 
 to Finance: Submit the PRQ for Finance approval. The Finance module 
 will handle bill-wise adjustments and payment execution. 
 Track status: 
 Monitor PRQ status (Pending Approval, 
 Approved, Paid) and reconcile with bank statements. 
 Key notes: 
 PRQ 
 generation is automatic; SRA users are responsible for review and 
 accuracy. 
 Any 
 changes required after PRQ creation should be done by reversing the 
 voucher and creating a corrected voucher (follow your organization’s 
 change control).

title: Buy Out
text:
Buy Out 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Buy Out 
 Purpose: 
 Record when a tenant sells the unit 
 to the developer and the agreed buyout amount. 
 Why it matters: 
 Buyout payments are controlled and 
 validated against the recorded buyout amount to prevent overpayment. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Ownership > Buy Out 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Select 
 Business Unit, Financial Year, Document Type, Document Date. 
 Choose 
 PTS Detail and the corresponding Annexure / Unit No. 
 Enter 
 Buyout Amount manually. 
 Save. 
 Validation: 
 Voucher Generation will validate that 
 payment does not exceed the buyout amount. Once buyout is completed, the 
 tenant cannot perform another buyout. 
 Select Annexure 
 Choose the appropriate 
 annexure from the list. 
 Add Buy Out Information 
 Click on '+Add 
 New Row' to input details for Buy Out. 
 Unit No: Enter 
 the unit number. 
 Annexure No: Enter 
 the annexure number. 
 List: Select the 
 list option. 
 Amount: Enter the 
 amount. 
 Submit the Information 
 Review all the 
 entered details. 
 Click on the 'Submit' 
 button to finalize the buyout document.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
text:
Frequently Asked Questions 
 FAQ" />
 Frequently 
 Asked Questions & Troubleshooting 
 Q: I cannot create a voucher — error 
 says “Buyout amount exceeded.” 
 Cause: Voucher 
 amount is greater than the recorded Buy Out amount. 
 Fix: Verify the Buy Out record ( SRA 
 > Ownership > Buy Out ) 
 and adjust the voucher amount or correct the Buy Out record if it 
 was entered incorrectly. 
 Q: Key Receipt not found for a unit 
 but rent needs to be processed. 
 Cause: Key 
 Receipt must be recorded before rent vouchers. 
 Fix: Record Key Receipt ( SRA 
 > Allotment > Key Receipt ) 
 with correct Key Type and Key Receipt Date. If rent was already paid, 
 treat as advance and reconcile with Finance. 
 Q: TDS computed is different from 
 Finance expectation. 
 Cause: Incorrect 
 TDS Nature or Payment Head mapping. 
 Fix: Confirm TDS Nature in voucher line and Payment Head > 
 Account Head mapping with Finance. Recreate voucher if necessary. 
 Q: Annexure unit is already tagged; 
 I need to move it to another annexure. 
 Cause: System 
 prevents re-tagging of units already linked to an annexure. 
 Fix: Use Annexure Amendment to update details or create a transfer 
 process per your governance policy. 
 Q: Documents uploaded but not visible 
 in Eligibility screen. 
 Cause: Documents 
 may be attached to PTS or Annexure lines incorrectly. 
 Fix: Verify attachments at the correct line item and re-attach 
 if necessary.

title: Owner Transfer
text:
Owner Transfer 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Owner Transfer 
 cum Payee Amendment 
 1. Owner Transfer – Ownership 
 When is it used? 
Owner Transfer (Ownership) is used when the legal ownership of 
 a unit changes permanently . 
 Typical scenarios: 
 Sale 
 of the unit to a new buyer 
 Transfer 
 of property due to inheritance or succession 
 Transfer 
 of ownership through legal settlement, merger, or court order 
 Why it 
 is required: 
 Ensures 
 the new legal owner is correctly recorded in the 
 system 
 Rent, 
 tax, and statutory liabilities are mapped to the correct owner 
 Required 
 for legal compliance, audit, and financial accuracy 
 System 
 impact: 
 Old 
 owner is replaced with the new owner 
 All 
 future rent collections and liabilities shift to the new owner 
 Legal 
 ownership records are updated 
 Example: 
 Mr. A sells his unit to Ms. B. An Owner 
 Transfer (Ownership) is processed so Ms. B becomes the new legal 
 owner and receives all future rent payments. 
 2. Owner Transfer – Nominee 
 When is it used? 
Nominee transfer is used when the legal owner remains the same , 
 but a nominee is added for representation or future reference . 
 Typical scenarios: 
 Owner 
 wants to nominate a family member 
 Estate 
 planning purposes 
 Compliance 
 with society or regulatory requirements 
 Why it 
 is required: 
 Records 
 nominee details without changing ownership 
 Helps 
 in succession planning 
 Does 
 not affect rent payment or legal ownership 
 System 
 impact: 
 Legal 
 owner remains unchanged 
 Nominee 
 details are stored for reference 
 No change 
 in rent payee unless separately updated 
 Example: 
 Mr. A remains 
 the legal owner but nominates his daughter as a nominee. An Owner Transfer 
 (Nominee) 
 is recorded. 
 3. 
 Rent on Behalf / Payee Amendment (OTRNT) 
 When is it used? 
Rent on Behalf is used when rent collection rights are transferred 
 to another person , but legal ownership does NOT change . 
 Typical scenarios: 
 Owner 
 authorizes another person to receive rent 
 Rent 
 is paid to a spouse, relative, trust, or company 
 Power 
 of Attorney cases 
 Tax 
 planning or banking convenience 
 Why it 
 is required: 
 Ensures 
 rent is paid to the correct payee 
 Maintains 
 accurate TDS deduction and reporting 
 Avoids 
 legal and payment discrepancies 
 System 
 behavior: 
 Transfer 
 Type is fixed as “Rent on Behalf (OTRNT)” 
 Legal 
 owner remains unchanged 
 Only 
 the rent payee details are updated 
 Process 
 flow remains same as Owner Transfer 
 Example: 
 Mr. A is the legal owner, but requests rent to be 
 paid to his wife. A Rent on Behalf (OTRNT) entry is created 
 so rent is credited to the wife while ownership remains with Mr. A. 
 In short, 
 Purpose: 
 Transfer ownership or rent collection 
 rights to another person (owner, nominee, or rent-on-behalf). 
 Why it matters: 
 Legal ownership and payee details 
 must be accurate for payments and legal compliance. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Ownership > Owner Transfer 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Two document 
 types are available: 
 Owner Transfer 
 Transfer 
 Types: Ownership, Nominee 
 All 
 existing functions remain unchanged 
 Rent 
 on Behalf / Payee Amendment – OTRNT 
 Transfer 
 Type: Rent on Behalf — set as default and field is disabled 
 Process 
 flow remains same as Owner Transfer 
 Use search to 
 pick Unit No. (shows Unit No., Society Name, Tenant Name, Annexure 
 Detail). 
 Choose Transfer 
 Type: Ownership, Nominee, or Rent On Behalf (fixed for Rent On 
 Behalf). 
 Enter New Owner 
 Name and Transfer Date. 
 Save. 
 Behavior 
 rules: 
 For 
 Ownership/Nominee transfers, payee name remains as in Annexure. 
 For 
 Rent On Behalf, payee name is replaced with the new owner name in 
 voucher generation.

title: Voucher Generation
text:
Voucher Generation 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Voucher 
 Generation 
 Purpose: 
 Voucher Generation is the core financial 
 process where all payments such as rent, brokerage, buyout, and site 
 expenses are processed. It generates accounting entries and handles 
 TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) liability. 
 Why it matters: 
 This stage integrates SRA workflows 
 with the accounting system. Voucher Generation creates the ledger entries 
 that Finance uses to approve and execute payments. If vouchers are incorrect; 
 accounting, TDS, and audit trails will be wrong. 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Payment > Voucher Generation 
 Prerequisites 
 (what must exist before you start): 
 Payment 
 Head Type, Payment Head Master, and Payment Schedule Master must be 
 configured. 
 Annexure 
 or Buy Out record must exist for tenant/buyout payments. 
 Sub-ledgers 
 for payees should be created (automatic if TDSonSRA is enabled). 
 Key 
 Receipt must be recorded for rent payments (unless special rules apply). 
 Detailed 
 Steps (step-by-step): 
 Navigate: 
 SRA 
 > Payment > Voucher Generation . 
 Header selection: 
 Business 
 Unit: Choose the BU that owns the transaction. 
 Financial 
 Year: Select the correct FY for accounting. 
 Document 
 Type: Choose the document type (system defined). 
 Document 
 Date: Enter the date of the voucher (affects accounting period). 
 Choose Document 
 Category: (this determines 
 which reference fields appear) 
 Voucher 
 Generation: For normal rent, brokerage, commission and recurring payments. 
 Transit 
 Rent: For rent collected by a third party on behalf of the tenant 
 (special handling). 
 Buy 
 Out: For buyout payments — when selected, you will choose Buy Out 
 No instead of Annexure. 
 Site 
 Expenses: For one-time site expenses (festival payments, site maintenance) 
 — annexure tagging is not required. 
 Reference 
 selection: 
 If Document Category = Voucher Generation 
 or Transit Rent:Select Annexure Detail (tenant reference). 
 If Document Category = Buy Out: Select 
 Buy Out No (buyout reference). 
 If Site Expenses: No annexure required; 
 proceed to payment head selection. 
 Apply Payment 
 Schedule: 
 Click 
 Payment Schedule and choose the template created in Payment Schedule 
 Master. The template pre-populates payment heads, basis, and default 
 amounts. 
 You 
 may modify amounts per line (Modified Amount) if required; the template 
 amount remains as original. 
 Payment Type: 
 Choose 
 Immediate Payment or Post Dated Cheque (PDC). This affects how the 
 payment is processed in Finance. 
 Select Payee(s): 
 Click 
 Select Payee to open the payee selection window. Choose single or 
 multiple payees as required by the schedule. 
 For 
 Rent On Behalf or Owner Transfer scenarios, ensure the correct payee 
 (new owner) is selected. 
 Detail lines 
 (for each payment head): 
 Payment 
 Head: Choose from Payment Head Master (e.g., Rent, Brokerage). 
 Period 
 Duration / From Date: Enter the period the payment covers (e.g., Apr 
 2025 – Jun 2025). 
 Modified 
 Amount: Optional override of template amount. 
 TDS 
 Nature: Select the TDS category (if applicable). The system will compute 
 TDS based on the payment head and TDS rules. 
 Account 
 Head: Populated from Payment Head Master; used for ledger posting. 
 Validation 
 & Non-Store Purchase (NSP): 
 In 
 all cases, a Non-Store Purchase entry must be recorded by debiting 
 the relevant expense heads and crediting the Tenant or Supplier Heads 
 to account for the TDS liability. 
 Attachments 
 & Remarks: 
 Attach 
 supporting documents (invoices, approvals) line-wise if required. 
 Enter 
 remarks for audit trail. 
 Save & 
 Post: 
 Click 
 Save to create the voucher. The system will generate accounting entries 
 and create a payment requisition record (if configured). 
 Review 
 the generated ledger entries (debit/credit) before forwarding to Finance. 
 Post-processing: 
 Payment 
 Requisition is created automatically and must be reviewed in SRA > 
 Payment > Payment Requisition. 
 Finance 
 will pick up the requisition for approval and payment execution. 
 Common validations 
 & errors: 
 Buyout 
 amount exceeded: Voucher generation will fail if the payment amount 
 exceeds the recorded buyout amount. 
 Missing 
 Key Receipt: Rent vouchers may be blocked if Key Receipt is not recorded. 
 TDS 
 mismatch: If TDS nature is incorrect, the computed TDS will not match 
 Finance expectations — coordinate with Finance for correct TDS codes. 
 Account 
 head missing: Payment Head Master must have a valid account head; 
 otherwise posting fails. 
 Best practices: 
 Use 
 Payment Schedule templates to reduce manual errors. 
 Always 
 preview ledger entries before finalizing. 
 Attach 
 approvals and supporting documents to each voucher line. 
 Coordinate 
 with Finance for TDS and GL mapping.

title: Key Receipt
text:
Key Receipt 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Key Receipt 
 Purpose: 
 To manage the process of residents handing 
 over their house keys for area demolition in preparation for redevelopment, 
 and moving to rental areas or receiving full settlement from builders. 
 Key Receipt is a critical milestone — rent processing depends on it. This 
 feature records the physical handover of keys from tenant to developer/authority. 
 Without Key Receipt, rent cannot be initiated (or is treated as advance). 
 Key Receipt Process Overview: 
 1. Preparation 
 for Redevelopment: Residents 
 prepare to hand over the keys of their houses. 
 2. Handover 
 of Keys: Residents 
 submit their keys to the designated authority for area demolition. 
 3. Relocation: Residents move 
 to rental areas provided by the builders or receive full settlement for 
 relocation. 
 Steps: 
 Where: 
 SRA > 
 Allotment > Key Receipt 
 Detailed 
 Steps: 
 Select 
 Unit No. ( search shows Unit No., Society Name, Tenant Name, Annexure 
 Detail). 
 Verify 
 tenant details. 
 Choose 
 Key Type (system defined: Rental or Settlement). 
 Enter 
 Key Receipt Date and Demolition Date (if applicable). 
 Save. 
 Important: 
 If Key Receipt is not recorded, voucher 
 generation for rent should not proceed.
